Lore's own pull requests. With the loop switched on, every open pull
request that code review has passed, whoever opened it, gets one
`auto-merge` run on the external floor. The run waits until CI is green,
no review thread is open, Lore's review stands approved on the head and
the pull request has been open for the minimum age. Red CI, a conflict
or open review goes to a new `auto-merge-fix` agent, which pushes
commits without rewriting history and answers each thread; its replies
are posted in the threads and the settled ones resolved, three rounds at
most. Then the `approve` station approves it, as the lore-reviewer App
when it is installed (#3307) and as Lore's own App otherwise. On a
branch whose rule asks for an app…

The Auto merge loop now does the work itself instead of only listing Lore's own pull requests. With the loop switched on, every open pull request that code review has passed, whoever opened it, gets one `auto-merge` run on the external floor. The run waits until CI is green, no review thread is open, Lore's review stands approved on the head and the pull request has been open for the minimum age. Red CI, a conflict or open review goes to a new `auto-merge-fix` agent, which pushes commits without rewriting history and answers each thread; its replies are posted in the threads and the settled ones resolved, three rounds at most. Then the `approve` station approves it, as the lore-reviewer App when it is installed (#3307) and as Lore's own App otherwise. On a branch whose rule asks for an app…

# Feature Specification: Lore merges on protected repos, and every PR knows what blocks it

## lore-reviewer App and the auto-merge loop

The `auto-merge` line (`libs/assembly-lines/src/floor-pipelines/auto-merge.yaml`, one run per `pr_url`) waits at `await-merge`, a human station the `pr-ready-check` sweep answers, and fixes nothing *(amended 2026-10-23: the `auto-merge-fix` agent with its `fix-pr` and `fix-replies` stations is gone; a loop pull request is rebased and repaired by the implementation loop on the pull request's own events, `specs/external-floor` FR12.19, and a person's pull request is the person's to fix)*. Each of these holds the wait, in order: a conflict or red CI; an open review thread, whether or not a review, re-check or reply run is still answering it; Lore's review n…

## Why

The implementation loop looked after its pull request only while its run
was open. The run parks at `await-pr`, which the `pr-ready-check` sweep
polls every two minutes, and the moment the pull request is green with
no open thread the run ends so the backlog slot frees. From then on
nothing of the loop watched the pull request: when main moved the branch
fell behind or conflicted, when main's CI changed the branch went red,
and the ticket's pull request sat there. The auto-merge loop (#3320) had
grown a fixer to cover this, `auto-merge-fix`, which merged the base in
and edited any author's branch. That is not its job: auto merge waits
and approves, and the loop that opened a pull request keeps it
mergeable.

## Decision

### Amendment 2026-10-23: the auto-merge loop

The approver setting and its two-key ceremony are gone. Approving and arming moved out of the post-review station into an **auto-merge loop** (`specs/protected-branch-merge`), switched per repo by `auto_merge.enabled` with one setting, `auto_merge.min_age_hours` (24 by default). ## lore-reviewer App and the auto-merge loop

The `auto-merge` line (`libs/assembly-lines/src/floor-pipelines/auto-merge.yaml`, one run per `pr_url`) waits at `await-merge`, a human station the `pr-ready-check` sweep answers, and fixes nothing *(amended 2026-10-23: the `auto-merge-fix` agent with its `fix-pr` and `fix-replies` stations is gone; a loop pull request is rebased and repaired by the implementation loop on the pull request's own events, `specs/external-floor` FR12.19, and a person's pull request is the person's to fix)*. With this change, the implementation loop makes the changes its reviewer asks for, the same way it fixes red CI. `await-pr` reads Lore's verdict on the head after CI. When the verdict asks for changes and no re-check is still running, it resumes `changes_requested` with reason `review_changes_requested`. The line routes that through `sync-pr` to `fix-ci`, under the same 3-round budget as red CI. The round brief carries the findings from Lore's newest review, its body and inline comments, under a "Lore's review asked for changes on <sha>" heading. {"answer":"Lore's auto-merge run sits at `await-merge`, a human station that the `pr-ready-check` sweep answers, and it fixes nothing itself. It keeps waiting while any of these holds, checked in this order:
1. The pull request has a conflict with its base, or CI is red.
2. CI is still running, or CI hasn't started in a repo that runs checks.
3. A review thread is open. This counts even if a review, re-check or reply run is still answering it.
4. Lore's review does not stand approved on the current head commit.
5. The pull request is younger than the minimum age, `auto_merge.min_age_hours`, which defaults to 24 hours. A pull request whose open time GitHub didn't report counts as old enough.

Once CI is green, no thread is open, the review is approved and the age is met, the `approve` station approves it. It approves as the lore-reviewer App if that is installed, and as Lore's own App otherwise.

The original version (#3320) sent red CI, conflicts and open review to an `auto-merge-fix` agent. That agent was removed on 2026-10-23 (#3376). The implementation loop now repairs and rebases its own pull requests, and a person's pull request is left for that person to fix. I didn't read the part of the spec that covers the exact wording of the review condition, so item 4 rests on the #3320 description and the spec's test names.","sources":["specs/protected-branch-merge/spec.md (section: lore-reviewer App and the auto-merge loop)","pull-3320 / commit d7ef8ddf0cfd3b4fcc6366bf42a11f59e466ca3c","pull-3376 / commit 1731e90c954231bfdb964b60658f31631dbf2301","adrs/ADR-051-protected-branch-approver.md","apps/stations/src/work/pr-ready-check/decide-merge-ready.test.ts"]}
